text: Argparse turns a script into a real command-line tool, with proper arguments and help text.
You create a parser, giving it a description that shows up in the automatic help message.
A positional argument, like name, is required and given by position on the command line.
[chuckle] Optional arguments start with dashes — times takes a number and defaults to one if omitted.
[sniff] A store-true flag like shout is a simple on-off switch, true when present, false when absent.
argparse handles all the parsing, type conversion, and validation for you.
Then you read the results as attributes — args dot name, args dot times, args dot shout.
[sigh] So this tiny tool greets someone a chosen number of times, optionally shouting.
[groan] argparse even generates a polished help screen automatically — it's how professional Python command-line tools are built.
Video 81 tackles the CSV module. Follow so you don't miss it.
